title: The Gale of Relief & The Coalition's Flight
subtitle: Nu'aym's Shrewd Diplomacy, Freezing Gale, and Dispersal
summary: Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud's diplomacy as the classical sirah tells it, Hudhayfah's night reconnaissance in Muslim 1788, the wind in the Quran and in Bukhari 4105, and the statement in Bukhari 4110 that the Muslims would now go to them.

sections.text: The classical sirah says that Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, of Ghatafan, came to the Prophet during the siege, told him he had accepted Islam, and was told to do what he could to divide the confederates. The conversations he is then said to have held with Banu Qurayzah and with Abu Sufyan are that biographical account. They are not the text of Muslim 1788, which is Hudhayfah's reconnaissance.

In that account he warned Banu Qurayzah that Quraysh and Ghatafan could leave them to face Madinah alone, and he warned the Quraysh that Banu Qurayzah were asking for hostages. The sirah says each side then distrusted the other. The wording of those warnings is not presented here as a sahih transcript.

Nu'aym then rode to Abu Sufyan and the Makkan chieftains, informing them that Banu Qurayza had secretly repented of their betrayal and promised Muhammad to seize high-ranking Makkan nobles as hostages to be handed over for execution. When Abu Sufyan sent an envoy to Qurayza proposing a coordinated assault on the following day, Qurayza replied that they could not fight on the Jewish Sabbath without first receiving Makkan hostages. Both camps concluded the other was treacherous, and the confederacy fractured from within.

On a night of piercing cold and howling gale winds, the Prophet ﷺ sought a volunteer to infiltrate the confederate camp. In the freezing darkness, exhaustion kept every companion glued to the ground until the Prophet called specifically upon Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. Handing him the assignment, the Prophet ﷺ commanded: 'Go and bring me news of the enemy, but do not provoke them or do anything until you return to me.'

Hudhayfah crawled across the trench into the Makkan lines, sheltered by divine warmth. He witnessed Abu Sufyan standing by a dying fire, shivering and calling out: 'O men of Quraysh! Let every man verify who sits next to him.' Hudhayfah swiftly grabbed the hand of the warrior beside him and asked, 'Who are you?' deflecting suspicion. Abu Sufyan then announced to his army that their pack-animals were dying, the weather had become unendurable, and Banu Qurayza had broken faith, ordering an immediate evacuation.

As the coalition hesitated, Allah unleashed His unseen forces. A furious east wind (Rih al-Saba) descended upon the plains of Madinah. The freezing tempest uprooted the confederate tents, overturned their iron cooking cauldrons, threw down their campfires, and whipped blinding sand into the eyes of their sentries. Seized by panic and spiritual dread, Abu Sufyan leapt onto his hobbled camel, whipping the beast to move before even releasing its tether.

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَاءَتْكُمْ جُنُودٌ فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا وَجُنُودًا لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا
'O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when armies came to resolve against you, and We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.' (Surah Al-Ahzab 33:9)

By morning the confederate camp had gone. Sulayman ibn Surad reported, in Bukhari 4110, that the Prophet said, 'From now we will go to attack them, and they will not come to attack us.' Bukhari 4118 is a different report: Anas saw the dust of Jibril's company as the Prophet set out for Banu Qurayzah. It is not this sentence.

references.title: The Holy Quran
references.author: Surah Al-Ahzab (33:9 & 33:25)
references.notes: Divine testimony to the unseen forces and the fierce wind that drove back the confederate army in rage.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.notes: Sulayman ibn Surad: 'From now onwards we will go to attack them, and they will not come to attack us.' Bukhari 4118 is the dust of Jibril's company on the march to Banu Qurayzah, and it is not attached to this sentence.

references.title: Sahih Muslim
references.author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 261 AH)
references.source: Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Ghazwat al-Ahzab wa Hadith Hudhayfah, Hadith 1788
references.notes: Detailed narration of Hudhayfah's nighttime reconnaissance into the enemy camp.
